newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Premier is first in Russian power succession line.
newsitem.headline: Premier is first in Russian power succession line.

text.p: Here are the rules of succession in Russia if President Boris Yeltsin's planned heart surgery goes wrong or if worsening heart problems prevent him from continuing his duties.
Under the constitution the Russian prime minister, currently Viktor Chernomyrdin, would run the country for three months if the president died or if he was found incapable of carrying out his duties.

"The president of the Russian Federation stops exercising his duties early if he resigns, shows a lasting inability to carry out his responsibilities due to bad health or if he is impeached," the constitution says.
The post-Soviet constitution, adopted in December 1993, gives the president strong powers, but makes impeachment -- a complicated, multi-stage procedure -- unlikely.
But Russian legislation does not cite any precise reasons why a president may resign.
It contains no procedures to determine that the president is incapable of carrying out his duties for health reasons.
But the constitution says the upper house of parliament should call an early election if the president dies, is incapacitated through illness or if he resigns.
"The day of the election should then be the last Sunday before the expiry of three months from the moment when the president quits," says the law on presidential elections.
The prime minister stands in for the president during this period, but he cannot dissolve parliament, call referendums of propose amendments or changes to the constitution.
Russian legislation does not specify the next in the line of succession if the acting president dies or steps down before an early election is held.
